vision: EXPLORE becomes a calm, fast, read-only discovery surface: title, search, one pill rail (Featured / New / Following), one deduped grid of one card type â€” keeper-led (avatar, name, bio, one stat), no villa wallpaper, no publish control panel. It sits on the cream #FCFAF5 canvas with ember #B85C38 as the only interactive color, gold reserved for focus rings, one guarded entrance animation, and every target >= 2.75rem. The data layer stops leaking private profiles, stops scanning 2000 rows per request, and stops fabricating per-rail stats. ME stops being a control panel: the Me tab lands on an identity-first page â€” portrait, name, three stewardship stats, 'Edit profile' + 'View my public profile', then quiet doors to settings (Airbnb pattern). Settings collapses from 9 tabs to 6; Security becomes the real home of MFA/password/export/delete/blocked/cookies instead of a 22-item brochure; Sharing becomes the single answer to 'who can see what'; Family and Subscription shed their marketing. A keeper lands on Me and feels 'this is my legacy', not 'these are my account options'. All iOS free-tier seals, Apple 1.2 blocking, and GDPR surfaces are preserved byte-for-byte in behavior.

doNotTouch: iOS free-tier seal (Apple 3.1.1, six-rejection saga): hideInNative on the Subscription tab (settings/layout.tsx:114), forced-free displayed plan on iOS (subscription/page.tsx:100-106), IAP_ENABLED/iapReady branches, iOS-hidden referral gate (:1139) â€” every merge/cut must preserve these byte-for-byte in behavior; no new surface may route iOS users toward /settings/subscription or pricing; /settings/sharing is a verified-safe relocation target.
excludeBlocked (directory-actions.ts:295-308) â€” Apple Guideline 1.2 blocked-user filtering: hoist/optimize to one fetch per request, never remove.
BlockedAccountsPanel (security/page.tsx:221) must stay mounted somewhere in Me (Apple 1.2 UGC compliance).

GDPR Art. 7/15/17 surfaces: ExportPanel, account deletion, and cookie-consent toggles (mp-cookie-consent/mp-cookie-analytics) must remain reachable within two taps; /settings/cookies must redirect, never 404, after the merge.
Every palace card must keep at least one route to /u/[username] â€” the SafetyMenu report/block chain depends on it; change 7 makes /u/ the primary destination, satisfying this.
Explore search â€” the page's one irreplaceable function; reduce chrome around it, never the capability.
NudgeProvider page="explore" and its data-nudge anchors: any anchor removed by the tab/section merge must have its nudge definition updated in the same commit or the 60+ guided tutorial breaks.

Behavior of publish/unpublish and passcode server actions (publishWing/unpublishWing/publishRoom/unpublishRoom, createPasscode/deletePasscode) â€” only the duplicate Explore UI dies; /settings/sharing remains the canonical surface.
summary: Explore and Me both predate the Atrium overhaul and it shows. Explore was a discovery page carrying a 520-line publish control panel (an exact duplicate of Settings > Sharing), three explainer cards that pushed every real palace below the fold, three near-identical rails with fabricated stats, and â€” worst â€” a genuine privacy leak: users who set their profile private still appeared in Trending and Newest. That leak ships first, alone. Then we delete the duplicates (~2,500 lines including a 1,089-line component that is verifiably dead code) and rebuild Explore as one search bar, one filter rail, one grid of keeper-led cards on the warm cream canon â€” faster, calmer, every tap target at least 2.75rem for the 60+ audience. Me stops being nine scrolling settings tabs: the tab lands on a page that shows your portrait, your name, what you have preserved, and two buttons â€” Edit profile and View my public profile (a link that today does not exist anywhere). Settings collapse to six honest doors; Security finally holds the actual security controls instead of marketing copy; Sharing becomes the one place that answers 'who can see what'; Subscription sheds 400 lines of re-selling. Nothing Apple-compliance- or GDPR-load-bearing moves out of reach: the iOS free-tier seal, blocking, export, delete, and cookie consent are all named untouchable. Four phases, 24 changes, roughly half of them pure deletion.
